_about: Scene 1 extract of every Bible entry the shot list draws on. Prefix wording for LOCKED entries is copied verbatim from the Drive bibles (only the bracketed character tag is renamed where the Sep 18 script renamed the character). PROVISIONAL entries contain only details stated in the script and must be approved by the producer before image batching.

cinematography_prefix.text: Cinematic tearjerker tone, emotionally intimate framing, soft natural light favoring dawn or dusk. Foil visible somewhere in frame — crumpled, glinting, or scattered nearby. Environment shows worn signs of habitation — blankets, bags, makeshift bedding — treated with visual dignity, not disorder. Camera lingers rather than cuts quickly, allowing emotional weight to build.

blocking_prefix.text: Composition follows dynamic symmetry principles — subject(s) positioned along a diagonal sightline rather than center-frame, with deliberate negative space.

rules: Describe drug items as objects (small blue pills, foil) — never name the substance in visual prompt text

global_negatives: no dead-center framing unless flagged as intentional
no clean or brand-new camping gear; tents show wear and dust
no high-contrast plastic or neon garbage bins

SOLEDAD_SUEY_SING.source: LOCATION BIBLE: [SOLEDAD STREET — SUEY SING BUILDING & DOROTHY'S PLACE] — producer's CORRECTED LAYOUT note
SOLEDAD_SUEY_SING.text: The Suey Sing Building on Soledad Street, Chinatown, Salinas: tan/cream single-story stucco building, weathered signage, boarded and graffiti-covered sections along the lower wall, no fence in front. The seven-story Moongate Apartments rise on its left. On its right, a dirt, weed and rock-filled field holds twenty weathered tents. Against the building's wall: a tent in each corner and a huge tarp-built two-unit structure between them, with shopping carts, bikes and belongings.
negatives: Moongate Apartments on the left of Suey Sing, never the right
no fence in front of the Suey Sing Building
do not fill in, build over, or remove the open field
do not merge the building-side encampment with the field encampment

DOROTHYS_PLACE.text: Dorothy's Place, directly across Soledad Street from the Suey Sing Building: two-story Spanish/mission-style building, yellow stucco walls, dark-red trim and support beams, upper wooden balcony with railing, green-trimmed windows, three recessed cubbyhole entrances at ground level, yellow brick wall topped with black steel spikes running left and right, a large shade tree, a utility pole standing directly in front near the entrance.
negatives: never remove the utility pole in front of Dorothy's Place
no swapping architectural styles with the Suey Sing Building
